ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a nitrogen molecule, N≡N, on the reactant side, plus three hydrogen molecules shown as H-H. An arrow points to the product side, where two ammonia molecules are shown, each with one nitrogen atom bonded to three hydrogen atoms. Reasoning: On the reactant side, the N2 molecule contains 2 nitrogen atoms, and the three H2 molecules contain 6 hydrogen atoms total. On the product side, the two NH3 molecules contain 2 nitrogen atoms total and 6 hydrogen atoms total. Since the number and kinds of atoms are the same before and after the reaction, the diagram illustrates conservation of mass.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: it shows nitrogen gas plus three hydrogen molecules reacting to form two ammonia molecules. Count atoms on the reactant side: 2 nitrogen atoms and 6 hydrogen atoms. Count atoms on the product side: two NH3 molecules contain 2 nitrogen atoms and 6 hydrogen atoms. Since the same atoms are present before and after the reaction, infer that the reaction illustrates conservation of mass; therefore, mass is conserved in chemical reactions.
